title: The client is billed 2 credits for a correction with no price shown anywhere in the flow
surface: Document viewer → Correct Info modal (client user)
whatYouSee: The modal explains what a correction does and how to phrase it, then you hit Apply Correction. Nothing mentions credits. The credits figure in the rail quietly drops by 2. If your balance or weekly cap is short, the only signal is a red error after you have already committed.
whyItsWrong: A targeted correction costs 2 credits and is charged to any billable client user before the model runs. Every other client-billable action in the product discloses its price up front — the agent run dialog prints "Costs N credits." for client viewers, and the agent cards show "N credits per client run". This surface is the one that stays silent, which reads as a hidden charge.
evidence: src/lib/actions/intel-actions.ts:404-409 — charged before the model call
fix: Thread the viewer role and balance down to the modal: src/components/client-rail.tsx already has both (isStaff at line 64, creditBalance at line 49), so pass a viewerIsClient flag and creditBalance into ClientDocuments → DocOverlay → CorrectInfoModal. In src/components/correct-info-modal.tsx, render "Costs 2 credits." next to the ⌘Enter hint at lines 113-116 using CREDIT_COSTS.targetedCorrection from src/lib/credits.ts (client-safe), matching the wording at src/components/custom-agents.tsx:1253, and disable Apply Correction with an inline shortfall message when the balance is below the cost.

title: One misclick on a trash icon destroys a LinkedIn seat — no confirm, no undo, no feedback if it fails
surface: Client settings /clients/[id]/settings — LinkedIn Employee Advocacy roster
whatYouSee: Each employee seat row ends in a small trash icon sitting right next to the pause icon. Clicking it deletes the seat immediately — no confirmation, no undo, no toast. The seat's LinkedIn sign-in goes with it. If the deletion fails on the server the row simply reappears after the refresh with no message at all.
whyItsWrong: Seats beyond the plan limit cost 100 credits each and removal is explicitly documented as no charge and no refund. Because the paid-seat test is "current count is at or above the limit", removing any seat from an over-limit roster means re-adding a person costs another 100 credits. So a stray click on a 16-pixel icon, two pixels from the pause control, can burn 100 credits with no prompt. The handler also awaits the action without inspecting the result or catching a throw, so an authorization or write failure produces no visible feedback whatsoever.
evidence: src/components/linkedin-seats-workspace.tsx:211 — onClick={() => remove(seat)} on the trash button (216), adjacent to the pause button (202)
src/components/linkedin-seats-workspace.tsx:89 — `await removeEmployeeSeatAction(...)` with no result check and no try/catch, then router.refresh()
src/lib/actions/seat-actions.ts:124 — "Remove a seat (no charge / no refund)."
src/lib/actions/seat-actions.ts:129 — requireSeatAccess throws (seat-actions.ts:30-34) rather than returning an error result
src/lib/credits.ts:107 — withinPlan = currentSeatCount < seatLimit, so re-adding after a removal charges again
fix: In src/components/linkedin-seats-workspace.tsx: gate remove() behind a two-step inline confirm (mirror the existing `gate` warning strip at lines 142-151 — set a `confirmingId` state, show "Remove Jane Doe? Seats beyond your plan cost 100 credits and re-adding will charge again." with Cancel / Remove) rather than deleting on first click. Then handle failure: wrap the call at line 89 in try/catch and also check `res.ok`, writing the message into the existing `error` paragraph at line 137 — note the action currently only ever returns ok:true or throws, so the catch is the part that matters. Separately, in src/lib/actions/seat-actions.ts:125-133 consider recording the charged amount on the seat at add time (line 98) so the confirm text can be accurate per seat, and/or refunding a charged seat on removal.

title: The client's headline credit number is labelled "credits available" but is not what they can spend — three surfaces disagree
surface: Client settings /clients/[id]/settings (Credits & usage card) and the client rail credits pill on every page
whatYouSee: The left rail pill reads "Credits 180". The settings card shows "180" in large type directly above the words "credits available". Then on the AI Agents page a badge says "0 credits available" and every Run button is dead. Same workspace, same second, two different "available" numbers.
whyItsWrong: The rail and the settings card render the raw stored balance. The number that actually gates spending is the balance clipped by whatever remains under the weekly and monthly caps — that is what the Agents page shows and what the charge transaction enforces. So the two most prominent credit numbers in the product are labelled with a promise the system will refuse to honour whenever a cap is binding.
evidence: src/components/credits-panel.tsx:120 — labelled "credits available" directly beneath it
src/components/client-rail.tsx:171 — desktop pill renders that raw balance
src/components/client-rail.tsx:207 — mobile pill, with aria-label "… credits remaining" (client-rail.tsx:203)
src/lib/credits.ts:324 — availableCredits() clips balance by weekLeft/monthLeft
src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/agents/page.tsx:207 — the Agents page uses the clipped figure
src/lib/credits.ts:257 — assessCharge enforces the same caps at charge time
fix: Compute the spendable figure once server-side and use it on all three surfaces. In src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:96 pass `availableCredits(credits)` (import from src/lib/credits.ts) instead of `credits.balance`. In src/components/credits-panel.tsx:119-120 make the spendable figure the headline under "credits available" and demote the raw balance to a secondary line ("180 on balance · 0 spendable until Monday") — the panel already receives the full ClientCredits doc, so it can call availableCredits itself. Leave the Agents-page badge (custom-agents.tsx:466) as-is; it is already correct.

title: Client Settings is a nine-section single-column stack ending in a panel whose only content is a sign-out button
whatYouSee: An admin scrolls past a brand-profile form, a credits panel with a ledger, an agent-access checklist, a scheduled-runs table, then two sections of channel cards — nine of them, most reading "Not connected" — then an auto-schedule toggle, then a meetings list, then an invite key, then a panel containing nothing but a Sign out button that also lives in the rail. No tabs, no anchors, no index. A client sees six of those nine sections.
whyItsWrong: Nothing is grouped by task and nothing is collapsed, so "where do I top up credits" or "where do I disconnect LinkedIn" is a scroll-and-scan exercise. The channels grid is the worst of it: connected and disconnected platforms render as identical full-height cards, so the one or two channels that matter are lost among the ones that are off. The page heading also mis-describes the page — it mentions channels, meetings and teammates, and says nothing about credits, agent access or scheduled runs.
fix: Split src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx into tabs (Profile / Channels / Credits / Automation / Team) using the segmented-control markup from src/components/progress-view.tsx:42-67 with the active tab in a `?tab=` param so it is linkable, and rewrite the PageHeader description at line 79 to name what is actually on the page. Inside src/components/integrations-tab.tsx partition each section's platforms on `integrationIsUsable` and render connected ones first as full cards, disconnected ones as a compact add-a-channel row that expands into the full card on click. Delete the Account card at settings/page.tsx:212-220 — LogoutButton already renders in the rail's AccountMenu (src/components/account-menu.tsx:114).

title: Hitting a spend cap never explains itself and offers no way forward
whatYouSee: Two thin meters: "Used this week 150 / 150" with a red bar, and "Used this month 150 / 400". No sentence anywhere. No reset date. No button to ask for more. The card's subtitle says AI actions spend credits without ever saying how many. The client is capped and the page acts as if everything is normal.
whyItsWrong: The wording the client needs already exists in code and is only ever shown after an action has already failed: the reset guidance ("It resets on Monday", "It resets on the 1st") lives inside the denial messages. The card itself never states a reset date, never says what is now blocked, and offers no route to request more — even though a support flow exists elsewhere in the shell. So a client cannot plan around a cap or understand why they hit one.
evidence: src/components/credits-panel.tsx:12 — UsageMeter renders label, spent/limit and a bar; no reset or explanatory text
src/components/credits-panel.tsx:115 — subtitle names the spending actions but no amounts
src/components/credits-panel.tsx:125 — the two meters, with no warning state at 100% beyond the bar turning red (line 28)
src/lib/credits.ts:263 — the Monday reset sentence, reachable only via a denial
src/lib/credits.ts:36 — CREDIT_COSTS, the full price list, never rendered as a list anywhere
src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:109 — the card is shown to client users too, so this is a client-facing surface
fix: In src/components/credits-panel.tsx: give UsageMeter (line 12) an optional reset line and render it under each bar — compute the next Monday / the 1st with the existing creditWeekKey / creditMonthKey helpers in src/lib/credits.ts. At pct >= 100, render a warning strip (same shape as the seat gate strip in src/components/linkedin-seats-workspace.tsx:142-151) naming what is blocked, with the existing ContactUsButton (variant="row") as "Request more credits" — it needs userName/userEmail, so thread them from src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:109. Add a collapsible "What actions cost" table rendered from CREDIT_COSTS and TASK_EXECUTION_COSTS so pricing is visible before the wall.

title: The auto-publish switch snaps back with no explanation, and Disconnect silently does nothing when it fails
surface: Client Settings → Integrations → connected platform card
whatYouSee: You toggle "Auto-publish scheduled content". It flips, then flips back on its own with no message, so you cannot tell a refusal from a network blip. Separately, you click Disconnect: the spinner runs, stops, and the card still says Connected — no error, no reason. For a client user this is guaranteed every time, because disconnecting is a staff-only operation on the server and the refusal is thrown away.
whyItsWrong: All three handlers swallow their errors. The auto-publish toggle catches everything and just reverts the optimistic state, so the user sees the switch move twice and is told nothing. Disconnect and the Google sub-service disconnect catch and discard with a comment claiming revalidation corrects the state, but nothing revalidates on the failure path — and since a client is never permitted to disconnect, they get a spinner and silence forever. The card already has an error slot that the manual-credentials form writes into; these three paths just don't use it.
evidence: src/components/integrations-tab.tsx:447-450 — where formError is already rendered for the manual form
src/lib/actions/integration-actions.ts:89-96 — deleteIntegrationAction starts with `await requireStaff()`, which throws "Forbidden" for a client
src/components/integrations-tab.tsx:362-371 — the Disconnect button is not gated on isAdmin, so clients see and can click it
src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:33-37 — a client user reaches their own settings page
src/lib/actions/integration-actions.ts:75-86 — setIntegrationAutoPublishAction throws on Unauthorized/Forbidden rather than returning an error
fix: src/components/integrations-tab.tsx: set `formError` from the caught error in handleAutoPublishToggle (line 218), handleDisconnect (line 231) and handleDisconnectSub (line 548), and render it in each card's action area the way the manual form already does at lines 447-450 (the Google card needs its own error slot — it has none). Keep the optimistic revert, just say why. Separately, either hide the Disconnect button for non-staff (add the isAdmin/isStaff condition already available in that component at line 735) or let clients disconnect their own integrations by relaxing deleteIntegrationAction in src/lib/actions/integration-actions.ts:93 to the same self-scoped check setIntegrationAutoPublishAction uses at lines 80-83.

title: The credit ledger is the only place that tells a client what anything costs
surface: Client settings (/clients/[id]/settings) → Credits & usage → Recent activity
whatYouSee: Ledger rows: “Copilot chat message −1”, “LinkedIn employee seat: Test Test −100”. The card subtitle above says only “AI actions (agent runs, copilot messages, task executions, doc corrections) spend credits”, with no amounts.
whyItsWrong: A client can only learn the price of an action by performing it and then reading the ledger. Every price exists in code already — it is simply never displayed before the charge.
evidence: src/components/credits-panel.tsx:115 — subtitle names the actions but no amounts
src/lib/credits.ts — CREDIT_COSTS holds every price (chatMessage: 1, and the rest)
fix: Render CREDIT_COSTS as a short price list in the Credits card (“Copilot message 1 · doc correction 2 · agent run 25”) and put the cost on each action’s own button, so the price is visible before the click, not after.
